, a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications, today announced new subgroup analyses from the

mutant (“MT”) cohort of the Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 study evaluating gedatolisib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (“ABC”). These data were presented by Dr. Barbara Pistilli, Head of the Breast Cancer Unit, Gustave Roussy, at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 today, Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 4:15 a.m. EST/10:15 a.m. CEST during a late breaking rapid oral presentation:

params.linkText: VIKTORIA-1: Updated results of a randomized, open-label, phase 3 study of gedatolisib (geda) + fulvestrant (fulv) ± palbociclib (palbo) vs standard of care in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer (ABC) (Study 2)

children: Gedatolisib plus fulvestrant with palbociclib (“gedatolisib triplet”) or without palbociclib (“gedatolisib doublet”) significantly improved median progression-free survival (“PFS”) compared with alpelisib plus fulvestrant in HR+/HER2-,
mutant ABC patients with and without liver metastases and those with or without visceral metastases:
In patients with evaluable disease, the gedatolisib-based regimens induced higher objective response rates (“ORR”) (confirmed and unconfirmed) and longer median durations of response in both the
mutant and wild-type cohorts compared to the control:

mutant cohort, the discontinuation rate of gedatolisib due to treatment-emergent adverse events (“TEAEs”) was 5% and 4% for the gedatolisib triplet and doublet, respectively, compared to a 19% discontinuation rate due to TEAEs for alpelisib. Grade 3 stomatitis with gedatolisib was transient. By the second cycle of treatment, less than 3% of patients had Grade 3 stomatitis, and all grade 3 events improved within 1-2 weeks. Discontinuations due to stomatitis for the gedatolisib triplet and gedatolisib doublet were minimal, 1% and 0%, respectively.

“The additional data from Study 2 of VIKTORIA-1 show consistent and significant clinical benefit for important sub-groups of breast cancer patients treated with gedatolisib regimens,” said Igor Gorbachevsky, Chief Medical Officer of Celcuity. “For patients who do not have liver metastases and received the gedatolisib triplet, the median progression-free survival was approximately 21 months, versus approximately 9 months for the alpelisib regimen. This is a particularly important result since patients with no liver metastases represent approximately 60%-70% of all patients treated in this setting.”

“Additionally, the median duration of response was over 19 months for the gedatolisib triplet in both the PIK3CA wild-type cohort, or Study 1, and the PIK3CA mutant cohort, or Study 2, compared to not evaluable for fulvestrant in the PIK3CA wild-type cohort and 7.5 months for alpelisib plus fulvestrant in the PIK3CA mutant cohort. To our knowledge, the gedatolisib triplet in each study demonstrated the longest median duration of response results ever reported for a therapeutic regimen used in the primary analysis for a Phase 3 trial in the second-line HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer setting.”
Dr. Sara Tolaney, Chief of the Division of Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, presented a comparative analysis of data for the gedatolisib regimens from the
wild-type cohort of VIKTORIA-1 and other regimens evaluated in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.

params.linkText: Gedatolisib (Ged) vs Other Regimens Post-CDK4/6i and Endocrine Therapy (ET) in PIK3CA Wild-Type (WT) HR+/ HER2- Advanced Breast Cancer (aBC): A Network Meta-Analysis (NMA)

children: Eight studies were included in this network meta-analysis comparing progression-free survival outcomes in randomized controlled trials of systemic treatments evaluated among patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer with CDK4/6 inhibitor experience and

wild-type tumors. This analysis found that the gedatolisib triplet and doublet each demonstrated statistically significant or numerically superior improvement in PFS and in progression-free survival rate at 6 months relative to the non-gedatolisib regimens evaluated. Of note, the analysis found that patients treated with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet were a statistically significant 2x and 1.5x more likely to survive without disease progression or death compared to imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, respectively.

Breast cancer is the second most common cancer and one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1 More than two million breast cancer cases were diagnosed globally in 2022.1 While survival rates are high for those diagnosed with early breast cancer, only approximately 30% of patients who are diagnosed with or who progress to metastatic disease are expected to live five years after their diagnosis.2 HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most common subtype of breast cancer, accounting for approximately 70% of all breast cancers.2

Celcuity is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications. The company's first FDA-approved product is REVTORPYK™ (gedatolisib), pan-PI3K and mTORC1/2 inhibitor that comprehensively blockades the PAM (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway. Its mechanism of action and pharmacokinetic properties are differentiated from other currently approved and investigational therapies that target PI3Kα, AKT or mTORC1 alone or together. A Phase 3 clinical trial, VIKTORIA-1, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with fulvestrant with or without palbociclib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, supported FDA approval of REVTORPYK for use in patients without a
mutation detected following progression on or after treatment with at least one line of endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting. Results for the

mutant cohort of VIKTORIA-1 have been released. VIKTORIA-2 is an ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial incorporating two independent studies, Study 1 and Study 2, in two separate cohorts of patients with ABC who are treatment-naive in the advanced setting. Study 1 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- ABC. Study 2 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus letrozole as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-sensitive HR+/HER2- ABC. A Phase 1/2 clinical trial, CELC-G-201, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with darolutamide in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, is ongoing. More detailed information about Celcuity’s active clinical trials can be found at ClinicalTrials.gov. Celcuity is headquartered in Minneapolis.
